submission.justification: Module-D3 has the highest light yield at 20% coverage (38 PE/MeV in the 2025 summary), but 30% of modules fail after 20 thermal cycles, which breaks the hard 5% limit, and failed modules cannot be replaced. Module-D1 passes thermal cycling (0.5%) but gives the lowest light yield (23.5 PE/MeV at 30% coverage). Module-D2 passes thermal cycling (2% failures, within the 5% limit) and gives 37.7 PE/MeV at 30% coverage, the highest light collection among the compliant designs. 30% is the upper coverage bound, and the meeting notes confirm enough feedthroughs for it. Cold electronics are validated for all designs.

requirements.requirement: Module must be one of the three candidate designs
requirements.evidence: Module-D2 is listed in candidate_specs.md (wavelength-shifting bar with SiPM readout).

requirements.requirement: At most 5% of modules fail after 20 thermal cycles (300 K to 87 K)
requirements.evidence: thermal_cycling_tests.md reports 2% failures for Module-D2 (40-module batch). Module-D3 (30%) and Module-D1 (0.5%) were checked separately; D3 is excluded.
Coverage set to 30%, the upper bound. Feedthroughs are sufficient for 30% per meeting notes 2026-01-20.

Simulation at 30% coverage gives Module-D2 37.7 PE/MeV, versus Module-D1 23.5 PE/MeV. Module-D3 is higher on paper (38 PE/MeV at 20% in 2025 summary) but is excluded by the thermal-cycling constraint. Result is the best compliant option.

requirements.requirement: Finish by submitting one recommended module design and coverage
